_metadata.artifact_kind_note: This is a hand-authored seed artifact for the no-network-access analysis sandbox. The github_api.available flag is false because GH_TOKEN is unset and the sandbox cannot reach https://api.github.com. The pulls[] array is NOT empty: it is populated by local-git reconstruction from the 6 observed merge commits on main, each carrying the subset of per-PR fields that local git evidence supports (number from 'Merge pull request #N' parsing, merge_commit_sha, merged_at, base.ref, head.sha, head.ref reconstruction from the merge commit's second parent, user reconstruction from the merging author identity, classified_category from PR-title heuristics, phase from inflection-date comparison, is_blitzy_actor and is_dependency_bot flags). Fields that require GitHub API access (draft state, labels, requested_reviewers, body, classified_category_source=linear_label, pr_commits_first_at_iso/pr_commits_last_at_iso, review timelines) are set to null and accompanied by per-field null_reason. When scripts/03_extract_pulls.py runs with GH_TOKEN set and network reachable, it overwrites this file with the full API-derived PR inventory; the run_id and extraction_timestamp will then reflect that execution. The semantic contract is preserved across both modes: pulls[] is the authoritative source of merged-PR count for M2 Flow Velocity, M4 Flow Active, M5 Flow Efficiency, M6 Flow Distribution, M7 Flow Time, and M10 per-actor attribution.
_metadata.schema_version_change_note: Bumped from 1.0.0 to 1.1.0 in CP2 remediation: pulls[] is now populated from local-git reconstruction in fallback mode rather than being empty. Field semantics, names, and types are unchanged; the populated entries follow the schema documented in per_pr_schema_documentation below.

github_api.endpoint_note: The 'state=all' parameter is REQUIRED. Per AAP §0.2.2 web-search insight, the GitHub Pulls API defaults to returning only open PRs; closed AND merged PRs MUST be retrieved for Flow Velocity (M2) and Flow Time (M7). Without state=all, both metrics would silently report zero.
github_api.supplementary_endpoints_note: Per AAP §0.2.1.2 these auxiliary endpoints are also consumed by scripts/03_extract_pulls.py to populate pr_commits_first_at_iso/pr_commits_last_at_iso (used by M4 Flow Active and M7 Flow Time), review-event timestamps (used by M4 ready-for-review bounding), and PR event timeline (used by M4 ready-for-review event detection). Their raw outputs are persisted to data/reviews.json and data/pull_events.json respectively.
github_api.unavailable_reason: GH_TOKEN environment variable not set or rate limit exceeded; analysis sandbox has no outbound network access for this seed run
github_api.fallback_note: When the API is unreachable, scripts/03_extract_pulls.py reconstructs PRs from merge commits on main: parse merge-commit subjects for 'Merge pull request #NN' patterns, walk the merge commit's parent branches to identify the first-commit-on-branch, and emit one pulls[] entry per merge. Ad-hoc merges without a 'Merge pull request #NN' pattern (e.g., manual local merges) are also emitted but with number=null, source_kind='ad_hoc_merge', and a body explanation. This local-git fallback gives the merge-commit-derived PR inventory; it cannot resolve PR-level fields that exist only on the GitHub side (draft state, labels, requested_reviewers, body content beyond what is reconstructed from the merge subject, classification by Linear label). Such fields are emitted as null with an explanatory null_reason field. The observed_merge_commits_on_main array below records the raw merge-commit inventory; pulls[] is the PR-shaped projection of it.

excluded_authors_note: Per AAP §0.5.3.3 Flow Velocity, dependency-bot authors are excluded. The single excluded entry is the dependabot[bot] GitHub App account whose presence is confirmed via .github/dependabot.yml (which declares the gomod, github-actions, and docker package-ecosystems Dependabot manages in this repository). Blitzy actors are NOT excluded: agent@blitzy.com is the canonical Blitzy engineering identity (included in Flow Velocity as the after-period engineering actor per AAP §0.5.3.3); 191547922+blitzy[bot]@users.noreply.github.com is the GitHub App auto-merge identity (included to the extent its PR-authoring activity represents engineering output by Blitzy per AAP §0.1.5).

excluded_authors_emails_verification.decision: Only dependabot[bot] is added to excluded_authors. blitzy[bot] is intentionally NOT excluded per AAP §0.1.5 (Blitzy carve-out).

blitzy_actor_emails_note: The canonical Blitzy engineering-actor identity is the union of agent@blitzy.com (primary, used by 512 of 538 commits) and 191547922+blitzy[bot]@users.noreply.github.com (auto-merge App identity, used by 5 of 538 commits). Per AAP §0.1.5, both are treated as the single 'Blitzy' row in any per-actor aggregation (Metrics 2, 4, 5, 6, 10). Verified via git log --all --pretty=format:%aE | sort -u against the 538-commit roster in data/commits.csv.

This is consistent with per_engineer.json#Blitzy.merged_prs_attributed_post_introduction_pr_numbers=[11,12,18,20,27] and per_engineer.json#michael.non_pr_direct_merges_post_introduction=1. per_pr_schema_documentation.schema_note: This block documents the per-PR object schema for downstream consumers (scripts/09_compute_metrics.py). When pulls[] is populated, every object MUST conform to this schema.

field_types.title: string
field_types.draft: boolean | null (null when not retrievable from API)
field_types.user: object { login: string, id: integer | null, type: 'User'|'Bot', email: string|null }
field_types.head: object { ref: string, sha: string, repo_full_name: string }
field_types.base: object { ref: string, sha: string, repo_full_name: string }
field_types.requested_reviewers: array of object { login: string, id: integer | null }
field_types.requested_teams: array of object { name: string, slug: string }
field_types.linked_linear_keys: array of string keys matching regex '[A-Z]{2,}-\d+'
field_types.classified_category: string enum: feature | defect | risk_compliance | tech_debt | unknown
field_types.classified_category_source: string enum: linear_label | conventional_commit_prefix | keyword_match | fall_through_to_unknown

classification_priority_per_AAP_0_5_3_7: 1. linear_label: if PR body or title contains a Linear ticket key [A-Z]{2,}-\d+ AND LINEAR_API_KEY is set, fetch the linked Linear issue's labels and apply user-defined rules.

2. conventional_commit_prefix: parse PR title for leading type per .github/workflows/semantic-pr.yaml: feat → feature, fix → defect, chore → tech_debt, refactor → tech_debt, exp → tech_debt, doc → tech_debt, test → tech_debt.

3. keyword_match: scan title+body for tokens: security|compliance|audit|sla|gdpr|pci|cve|vulnerability → risk_compliance; bug|fix|regression|hotfix → defect; refactor|tech debt|cleanup|rename|format → tech_debt; feature|add|support|enable → feature.
4. fall_through_to_unknown: when none of the above resolve.
per_pr_schema_documentation.phase_assignment_rule: phase=baseline if created_at < inflection_date_utc (or merged_at when created_at unavailable in fallback mode); phase=post_introduction if >= inflection_date_utc AND <= analysis_period_end; phase=outside_window otherwise.

observed_merge_commits_on_main_note: Authoritative count of explicit merge commits on main, extracted via 'git log main --merges --pretty=format:%H|%aI|%s'. Five of the six reference a numbered PR (#11, #12, #18, #20, #27); the sixth is an ad-hoc local merge without a PR number reference. IMPORTANT: in fallback mode this count is treated as the lower bound on the merged-PR-equivalent count for M2 Flow Velocity. Squash-merged PRs (the default in GitHub for many workflows) do NOT appear as merge commits at all — they appear as single commits with their original subject preserved. The exact merged-PR count requires GitHub Pulls API access; without it, M2 reports Medium confidence with this caveat surfaced in the report's Risk Assessment.

observed_merge_commits_on_main_phase_dis.note: All 6 merge commits fall after the inflection point 2026-02-25T02:58:59Z. The baseline phase (2026-02-23T05:19:38Z to inflection) contained only a single commit on main and zero merge commits.

summary.merged_prs_count_semantic_note: merged_prs_count counts every closed merge-commit-derived PR-like entry, including the ad-hoc merge. This is the merge-commit-fallback semantic for M2 Flow Velocity (AAP §0.5.3.3) when the GitHub Pulls API is unreachable. The breakdown distinguishes the 5 numbered PRs from the 1 ad-hoc merge so consumers can choose the stricter PR-only semantic (5) or the inclusive merge-commit semantic (6) as appropriate.
summary.closed_without_merge_prs_count_note: Closed-without-merge PRs are server-side only and not observable in local-git fallback. The fallback effectively reports zero unless an API-enabled run populates this.
summary.draft_prs_count_null_reason: Draft state is server-side only; cannot be retrieved in fallback mode.
summary.excluded_dependency_bot_prs_count_note: Zero dependabot[bot] PRs reached main during the analysis window. The dependabot[bot] account has 7 commits on dependabot/* feature branches but no merges to main.
summary.blitzy_authored_prs_count_note: PRs #11, #12, #18, #20, #27. The Blitzy actor union per AAP §0.1.5 includes both agent@blitzy.com (direct authoring) and 191547922+blitzy[bot]@users.noreply.github.com (auto-merge).
summary.human_authored_prs_count_note: The single ad-hoc merge ad44713 by michael@blitzy.com. ajay-blitzy's three direct-to-main chore commits are not PR-derived merge commits and are not counted here.
summary.merged_to_other_branches_prs_count_note: Zero observed in fallback mode; an API-enabled run would also enumerate release/* branch merges if applicable. The release-please.yaml workflow creates release/* branches on a tag basis, so cross-branch PR merges are uncommon in this repository.
summary.summary_note: Counts use the merge-commit-fallback semantic. merged_prs_count=6 matches the M2 Flow Velocity aggregate 6 merges / 6 windows = 1.0 per window. The 5 numbered + 1 ad-hoc breakdown above lets the renderer disaggregate by source if a stricter PR-only semantic is required. Per the CP2 review item, pulls.json, metrics.json#m2 (value=1.0, six merges over six windows), and per_engineer.json (Blitzy: 5 PRs; michael: 1 ad-hoc merge; ajay-blitzy: 0) are now internally consistent.
summary.prs_per_2week_window_baseline_note: Baseline phase spans only 2026-02-23 → 2026-02-25 (≈ 2 days). No full 2-week window fits in this range, so the per-window array is empty by definition. Per AAP §0.5.3.4 Flow Predictability, fewer than 4 windows triggers 'Insufficient signal — fewer than 4 windows' for M3 in the baseline phase.
summary.prs_per_2week_window_post_introduction_n: Post-introduction phase spans 2026-02-25 → 2026-05-21 (≈ 86 days, ≈ 6 two-week windows). Each entry reports the merge-commit-fallback per-window count alongside the PR numbers (or ad-hoc merge SHA) that fall in the window. When the API is reached, this array will be replaced with API-derived counts that may differ slightly because squash-merged PRs become visible.

rule_compliance.rule_1_data_provenance: Every numeric value in this artifact is derived from a single named extraction command. The pulls[] array is the result of local-git reconstruction from 'git log main --merges --pretty=format:%H|%aI|%aE|%s' plus per-merge subject parsing. The blitzy_actor_emails and excluded_authors lists are derived from 'git log --all --pretty=format:%aE | sort -u'. No estimation, extrapolation, or fabrication.
rule_compliance.rule_3_confidence_transparency: When this artifact's pulls[] array is populated via local-git reconstruction (current state), downstream metrics M1/M2/M4/M5/M6/M7 inherit Medium confidence at best because the reconstruction cannot resolve draft state, labels, requested_reviewers, body content, or per-PR commit timelines. The downstream metrics.json renderer surfaces this in the report's Risk Assessment section.
rule_compliance.rule_4_internal_consistency: _metadata.inflection_date_utc=2026-02-25T02:58:59Z is identical to data/inflection.json#date_utc. _metadata.run_id=ff490c72-43fb-4c05-b466-b9355cab917f is identical to the run_id in data/environment.json and data/inflection.json (single-run correlation per the Observability rule). summary.merged_prs_count=6 matches both metrics.json#m2.merge_commits_total=6 and per_engineer.json (Blitzy: 5 + michael: 1 ad-hoc = 6). summary.blitzy_authored_prs_count=5 matches per_engineer.json#Blitzy.merged_prs_attributed_post_introduction=5.
rule_compliance.rule_5_reproducibility: The exact endpoint string in github_api.endpoint plus the fallback method in github_api.fallback_note together specify how to re-derive this artifact from scratch. The Reproducibility Appendix in acceleration-report.md will reference both.
